import pandas as pd


def run(inputs: dict) -> dict:
    target = inputs["target_snapshot"].copy()
    cdc = inputs["cdc_events"].copy()
    watermark = inputs["watermark"].copy()

    # Watermark is a single row with column 'high_ts'
    high_ts = watermark["high_ts"].iloc[0]

    # 1. Keep only events strictly after the watermark (idempotent replay guard)
    filtered = cdc[cdc["event_ts"] > high_ts].copy()

    if filtered.empty:
        cols = ["product_id", "name", "price", "last_event_ts"]
        return {"new_snapshot": target[cols].reset_index(drop=True)}

    # 2. Per product_id pick latest event by (event_ts, event_seq), deterministic tie-break.
    filtered = filtered.sort_values(
        by=["product_id", "event_ts", "event_seq"],
        ascending=[True, False, False],
        kind="mergesort",
    )
    latest = filtered.drop_duplicates(subset="product_id", keep="first")

    # Work on the snapshot indexed by product_id for easy upsert/delete.
    snap = target.set_index("product_id")

    for _, row in latest.iterrows():
        pid = row["product_id"]
        op = row["op"]
        if op == "D":
            if pid in snap.index:
                snap = snap.drop(index=pid)
        else:
            # Upsert name/price and set last_event_ts = event_ts
            snap.loc[pid, "name"] = row["name"]
            snap.loc[pid, "price"] = row["price"]
            snap.loc[pid, "last_event_ts"] = row["event_ts"]

    new_snapshot = snap.reset_index()
    new_snapshot = new_snapshot[["product_id", "name", "price", "last_event_ts"]]

    return {"new_snapshot": new_snapshot}
